[size=150][b]Lionheart Fixt 0.27.0 - What the Thieves Say[/b][/size]

Enemies get something to say, and Fernand Desoto finally gets a way back.

[b]Hover text, one voice per family and a sub-bank per role[/b]

[b]67 cans, 71 lines, three families.[/b] The text floats over the creature's head, not in the combat log.

| family | shared | sub-banks | cans |
|---|---|---|---|
| thieves | 8 | boss 5, archer 5, melee 5 | 36 |
| English soldiers | 8 | officer 5, archer 5, melee 5 | 24 |
| Snakebreed | 7 | venom 5, summoner 4, boss 4, drone 5 | 9 |

A creature draws from its family's shared lines [b]plus the sub-bank for its own role[/b], so a thief
archer picks from thirteen and a thief boss from a different thirteen. The boss gives orders -- *"Hold
him! He is worth more breathing!"* -- while the archer talks about range -- *"Keep your distance from
him!"*. An English officer shouts *"Not one step back, do you hear me!"*; his archers call *"Nock and
draw!"*. The Snakebreed hiss: *"Ssssoft thing. Warm thing."*

Roughly [b]one attack in four[/b] carries a bark, and the line is drawn fresh each time.

[b]The mechanism is the game's own.[/b] 21 shipped cans already float a dialogue node over a creature with
[i]CDisplayDialogBalloonAction[/i] -- 18 sewer thieves and three guard dogs. Those guard dogs showing
[i]Guarddog[/i] node [i]10 Growls[/i] are also the precedent for a creature with [b]no speech[/b] and for a stage
direction as the whole line, which is what the Snakebreed use.

[i]Include In Log=0[/i] throughout, deliberately. The log is where this game puts narration -- 222 uses of
[i]CPrintCombatTextAction[/i] saying things like *"You discover a treasure buried in the ground"* -- so
creature speech there would read as the narrator rather than the enemy.

The three [i]Snakebreed Summoner[/i] cans are skipped: their attack slot already carries a
[i]CAddTemporaryAIAction[/i]. Their sub-bank sits in the tree unused, against the day they get one.

[b]Fernand Desoto can be taken back[/b]

Three earlier releases tried to fix this and all three failed the same way: they tried to make [b]one
dialogue node[/b] serve both the following and the released state.

| | what it did | why it failed |
|---|---|---|
| 0.25.3 | gave the node a dismiss and a rejoin, ungated | a dismissed Fernand still offered to be dismissed |
| 0.25.4 | gated the pair on a new scripting variable | the variable was never written -- the save proves it absent |
| 0.25.7 | found the node was a [b]balloon[/b] with no reply list at all, and made it a conversation | necessary, but the broken gating survived it |

[b]Cervantes has worked since 2003 and does none of that.[/b] He has a node called [i]3 Return after release
as a companion[/i], both replies ungated, and two maps carry an interaction specifier pointing straight at
it. The state is encoded by [b]which node the specifier opens[/b], not by a flag. Grumdjum uses the same
shape, and [i]666 Rejoin[/i] is the Knight of Saladin's version.

Fernand had a node for *following* and none for *released*. Three releases of gating were an attempt to
simulate a node that was simply missing.

Now:

| state | his interaction opens | what it offers |
|---|---|---|
| following | [i]100 companion banter[/i] | *Wait here, Fernand* -- releases him, then points his specifier at 103 |
| released | [i]103 fernand waiting[/i] | *Walk with me again* -- recruits him, then points it back at 100 |

Each swap runs from a [i]CCannedObject[/i] fired by [i]CUseCannedActionAction[/i], because a tree may not name
its own file, and the swap is copied field for field from the [i]fernand joins you[/i] relay already working
in the same map. The scripting variable is deleted.

Nothing now depends on [i]$Instigator[/i] resolving in that conversation, on a new attribute being writable
against an existing character, or on how the player dismissed him.

[b]What the companion audit missed, and why it matters[/b]

The audit that cleared Grace, the Goblin Girl and Grumdjum scanned [b]only this project's files[/b].
Cervantes is pure vanilla, so the working reference implementation for exactly this problem sat outside
the search path while three worse answers were invented against it.

A sweep asking *"how does this game do X"* has to include vanilla, not just what the mod has already
touched. That is now written into the project's own notes.

[b]Needs a fresh approach to those areas[/b]

Both halves are [b]can and entity changes[/b], so they reach creatures and interactions created after the
install:

- the barks want a save that has not entered the sewers, the Slave Pits, the bonus level, act 7's
  shrine or the Snakebreed's ground
- [b]Fernand needs a character who has not yet recruited him[/b] -- his interaction specifier is entity
  state and is snapshotted on first visit

[b]Fixt[/b] is a cumulative restoration-and-repair mod for Lionheart, after Fallout Fixt.

Download, unzip, run [i]Mod Manager.bat[/i].

https://github.com/EricHype/LionheartFixt/releases/tag/v0.27.0
